title: Plain parallel Pollard rho on P-256 (no negation map) with a deterministic round meter

claims.statement: For the uniform full-production P-256 target Q=[x]P, the classical cold attack in proof.md (plain R=2048-adding parallel Pollard rho with distinguished points, no negation map or automorphism classes, start-replay recovery, and a round/event meter) halts on every run after at most W_max < 2^130.4566 target-group-operation equivalents under the protected C=1000 normalization, with all P-256 arithmetic charged through itemised analytic instruction allowances (M=512, A=64, I=2^19 per field operation). It succeeds with probability at least 0.39 under the disclosed random-mapping heuristic H1 with a factor-2 margin (kappa=2) in the birthday constant. Peak memory < 2^99 bytes; preprocessing < 2^34.2 units, included; no nonuniform advice. The submitted rational bound is justified by the exact inequality W_max^100 <= 2^13047 checked in experiment.py. Not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Production curve checks and exact rational ledger/score inequality; end-to-end toy runs of the specified algorithm on small prime-order a=-3 curves measuring success, wrong outputs and the empirical birthday constant kappa.
